items.title: 60322_John Bubbles oral history interview
items.q: Tom Patricola, the dancer, Jack Donahue. Look, we had a big bill, eight acts

ctx.x: About three months after we played the Columbia Theater we played the Palace and no negro played that Palace, man, for months and months, they told me we wouldn't get in there. We played it. In less time -- they were still getting in the Palace when we played it. However, we played the Palace. First Negro act held over a second week in the Palace Theater. We went on the stage with such people like Ray Samuels, Clayton Jackson and (Jimmy) Durante, (Fred) Warings Pennsylvanians,

Tom Patricola, the dancer, Jack Donahue. Look, we had a big bill, eight acts and after the first week we had to be placed on No. 2, next to closing, about the third act. They had to put us on next to closing because nobody wanted to follow us. We turned out to be the next to closing act from that point on.
Then we got on the Orpheum circuit.
